_comment: ONE binding per noun. This is the file that replaces Cucumber's step definitions,
and the whole bet is that it grows with the app's vocabulary rather than with the spec.
Every value below is copied from snip-it frontend/e2e/editor.spec.ts on origin/dev —
nothing here is invented, so the generated tests can be diffed against the real ones.
region:WordTrack and region:CutStatus are DELIBERATELY ABSENT. The real tests reach
that content with a bare getByText / regex because the app gives those areas no
accessible name at all. Leaving them out is the honest result: the generator refuses
and names the missing noun, instead of guessing a locator. That refusal is the spec
constraining the app, which is the property Gherkin never had.
⚠️ THE NOUN NAMESPACE IS GLOBAL ACROSS APPS, and this file is now the evidence.
snip-it's page:Home is './' and macro-metrics' home is '/macro-metrics/'. Writing
page:Home in the macro-metrics corpus therefore emits page.goto('./') — a test that
RUNS, against the wrong app, with no unbound-noun warning. The macro-metrics nouns
below are prefixed by hand to dodge that, which is not a design, it is a habit.
Measured, not assumed: prose-audit.js --demo-collision prints the emitted line.
(button:ToggleTheme is a near-miss the other way — both apps happen to label it
'Toggle Theme', so one shared binding is correct today by coincidence, not by rule.)
_comment_macro_metrics: macro-metrics, read off origin/main@89053e6 — nothing invented, same rule as above.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT, each an honest refusal rather than a gap:
link:Presets / link:Compare / link:Indicators — the AC says 'anchor links';
StickyNav.tsx renders <button onClick={scrollIntoView}>. Binding these to the
buttons would let the corpus absorb the divergence, which is the Gherkin failure.
ratio:Errored, ratio:OneErrored — macro-metrics has ZERO .spec.ts files, so no
route-mock helper exists to bind a `given` to. Refuse, do not invent one.
button:Range1y … button:RangeMax — these have PERFECT accessible names ('1y' …
'Max'). They are absent because NINE PresetCards each render all six, so the
noun names 9 elements and any locator is ambiguous under Playwright strict mode.
The notation has no cardinality; this is where that stops being a nit.
card:<any one preset card> — PresetCard's root is role='button' with NO accessible
name (its text is dynamic title/value), so a single card cannot be addressed.
